nodes.s: MCP client · stdio shim by default
d: Launches pseudolife-mcp as a per-session stdio subprocess
Alternative: direct HTTP transport straight to /mcp
SessionStart hook injects the memory briefing
Wired by ops/install --client codex
Hooks: the plugin's own hooks.json when the Codex plugin is installed, else a managed ~/.codex/hooks.json (install --codex-hooks auto|manual|plugin|skip)
Any client without streamable-HTTP support goes through the shim
Wired by ops/install --client gemini (-s user scope, -e writer id)
No hook system — standing ~/.gemini/GEMINI.md carries the loop
Talks only to /ui/* and /api/*
Bearer token kept in localStorage (pl_token); a 401 shows the refusal with a token prompt
Deliberately bundles no MCP server (avoids duplicate tool namespaces)

Manifest carries no version: Claude Code caches each marketplace commit in its own folder, so updates install beside running sessions; the release is plugin/release.json, pinned to pyproject by test_plugin_packaging
Served straight from master via marketplace.json — no publish step

hooks.json wires eight bash scripts: session-start (twice, the second for memory-policy), coordination-start, user-prompt-submit, coordination-prompt, session-end, stop-wake, subagent-board and subagent-board-guard (a PreToolUse guard on memory_agents / memory_message); every entry's commandWindows is lifecycle.ps1, Codex's native-Windows override
GET /api/hook/session-start → stdout becomes session context
On resume or compact the daemon serves only drift notices, the episode-handle line and a briefing pointer (after a compaction also hook-instructions.md); the memory-policy request forwards source too
Fail-open: daemon down → friendly fallback, still exit 0
Payload capped at 9,500 chars (client caps stdout at 10k)

Board state is a sibling SessionStart hook, coordination-start.sh: the per-process shim digest-key record, the <key>.reprint flag on resume / compact / clear, and the board check-in from GET /api/hook/coordination-start (2 s)
Sources session-start.sh memory-changes: one GET /api/hook/memory-changes per turn (2 s cap, no retry), printing only when lessons or other sessions' status notes landed since the session's last note
Cursor in <digest dir>/<sha256(session id)>.mark, saved only after printing, so a missed note is asked for again next turn
The note's reminder tail keeps recall-before-review; silent on any failure, always exit 0

Coordination digest is a second UserPromptSubmit hook, coordination-prompt.sh: prints the shim's per-session digest when its watermark passed the shared .seen marker (or once after SessionStart's .reprint flag), leaves the <key>.turn stamp the park gate reads and one ledger line per firing; local files only, no daemon call
POST /api/hook/session-end closes the session episode
Ownership-guarded: only clears the active-session pointer it owns

First, before the connection checks and any network call (plugin SessionEnd hooks get 1.5 s): on /clear or /resume confirms the process's digest-key record for the ending session (rewriting one that is not) and leaves the handoff claude-<CLAUDE_PID>.switch: time, the process's creation identity, the ending session's key

On by default since 2026-09-28; off on a PSEUDOLIFE_AGENT_WAKE_HOOK of 0/false/no/off or a PSEUDOLIFE_AGENT_COORDINATION set to anything but 1/true/yes/on, checked in the hooks.json command before bash reads the script
async + asyncRewake: waits after each turn on the session's coordination digest; exit 2 wakes an idle session

v49: fires only on a rung ring the daemon decided (<key>.ring past .seen, written by the shim for rung mail) with the digest past .seen and mail listed; chatter, withheld mail and plain mail to a session that never parked never wake (urgent mail to it is rung; since 2026-10-02 a leftover nudged marker is no ring); the wait ledger line carries the ring's reason; one lease per session, at most 20 wakes an hour

While waiting it renews a 60 s local listener lease every poll (the daemon rings only an address with a live wake path); after a wake fires, one background POST /api/hook/woke (2 s) records it for wake-precision stats

v49 park gate, before the wait: unless stop_hook_active, with <key>.agent present, one 2 s request to GET /api/hook/park-gate?agent=<id>&since=<the .turn stamp coordination-prompt.sh leaves>; block ends the turn at once (exit 2) with the daemon's message, once; allow, no address or no answer arms the wait

Codex loads the same hooks.json and gets only the park gate on every platform (off on an explicit PSEUDOLIFE_AGENT_WAKE_HOOK or PSEUDOLIFE_AGENT_COORDINATION of 0/false/no/off): on Windows lifecycle.ps1 -Event Stop, on macOS and Linux this script in Codex context (PSEUDOLIFE_CODEX_HOOK=1 or PLUGIN_ROOT equal to CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT), resolving the daemon from the managed connection file as coordination-start.sh does; a block is {"decision":"block","reason":...} on stdout with exit 0 as Codex documents, plus the gate ledger line, and the wait is never armed (the doorbell is Codex's wake)

SubagentStop (argument subagent-stop; lifecycle.ps1 -Event SubagentStop on Windows) runs the same gate for a Codex child thread, keyed by the payload's agent_id (the child's MCP threadId, a canonical lower-case UUID; never the root session_id), with no turn stamp; in Claude Code it does nothing

v50: keeps a Claude Code session's board children current: SubagentStart adds, SubagentStop removes, one 2 s POST /api/hook/subagent naming the session's address (<key>.agent, found as stop-wake.sh finds it) and the payload's agent_id and agent_type; both entries are async in hooks.json (the answer is ignored)

Top-level payload keys only (an escaped copy inside last_assistant_message never matches); a malformed id sends nothing, a malformed type is left out; runs only in a hook Claude Code started for this very session
Fails open: exits 0 and prints nothing on every path, so a down daemon or a refused bearer never holds a subagent back

Codex loads the same hooks.json: a no-op there (lifecycle.ps1 -Event SubagentBoardStart|SubagentBoardStop exits at once; this script exits in Codex context); the shim links Codex's native subagents to their parent instead; ops/setup-codex-hooks.py treats both events as optional, like Stop
/dream: agent-led consolidation via memory_dream (+ deep mode)
/memory-status: /health + memory_stats + console pointer
Fresh upstream HTTP connection PER TOOL CALL — dodges idle-connection reaping that used to hang post-pause calls
Probes /health; spawns `pseudolife-mcp serve` detached if daemon absent

A daemon it must not spawn (non-loopback URL, or PSEUDOLIFE_MCP_NO_SPAWN) that misses a 5 s wait starts the session degraded: initialize + tools/list from the per-URL handshake cache (handshake-cache/ under PSEUDOLIFE_AGENT_STATE_DIR, else ~/.pseudolife-mcp), calls retried, a /health watcher emits tools/list_changed on recovery

X-PL-Session = Claude Code's session id when the writer is Claude Code (joins the hook's root), else one uid per process; opens no episode (the daemon lazy-opens on the first write); closes only its own key at exit
Re-emits tools/list_changed downstream after memory_toolset tier changes
Optional channel mode isolates the earlier handshake and serializes labeled events beside tool replies; real-host delivery requires explicit opt-in and verification

By default asks /api/hook/coordination-start at startup and builds its coordination adapter (Codex: per-thread registry) only where the daemon serves its bearer the board; appends the compact board check-in to the MCP instructions only when the adapter is up (or its registration is being retried after the daemon said yes). A startup registration or board check the daemon did not answer is retried in the background by _LateBoardAdapter, which stands in for the adapter until one lands (for Codex, _LateCodexRegistry builds the per-thread registry on a later yes)

A process serving many conversations (writer id claude-desktop or tunnel, or PSEUDOLIFE_MCP_SHARED_HOST not off) binds no coordination identity, refuses memory_message / memory_agents update, claim and release with a pointer to a per-session server, and prepends that advice to its instructions; its memory_agents list shows open sessions only
(no arg) → shim · serve → daemon · embedded → legacy v0.1 stdio · channel → optional preview transport

briefing / prompt-hook / doctor / backup / export / import / board-audit / coordination-recovery / wait-mail / lease / doorbell-prompt-seen / episode-start / episode-end subcommands; host lifecycle: update · connect / invite / pair / expose / tunnel / move
Heavy imports deferred into serve/embedded branches — shim start is near-instant

GET /api/briefing → markdown; --hook-json: GET /api/hook/session-start → hookSpecificOutput JSON; --coordination prints the board check-in from /api/hook/coordination-start instead, empty where the board is off
Never auto-starts the daemon; prints nothing on any failure

prompt-hook: the plugin's per-turn memory-change note (GET /api/hook/memory-changes, 2 s, redirects refused) with the same <digest dir>/<sha256(session id)>.mark cursor, saved only after printing; imports no shim or httpx (URL and redirect helpers come from the stdlib-only daemon_url.py), since it runs every turn
Wired by ops/install-hook for non-plugin installs
Superseded by daemon-owned session episodes (2026-06-30)
install-hook strips it from old installs; still shipped for compat

nodes.s: pseudolife-mcp export / import · logical bank transfer
d: ZIP of JSONL (one per table) + manifest — decoupled from Postgres major version and deployment tier, unlike pg_dump's physical backup
Export is a live-safe REPEATABLE READ snapshot; import fills a fresh bank only, inside one transaction, ids/HLC/embeddings verbatim
Carries entry dream state but excludes the acknowledgement secret; an imported bank creates its own token identity
Operational coordination_agents, coordination_messages, the coordination_events audit log and the v45 lease tables never enter portable knowledge exports; full database backups retain them
Serving telemetry stays behind too: retrieval_events/retrieval_uses, slot_reads, lesson_search_events, the dream-run journal, and the outcome_signals.used_ids column (EXCLUDED_COLUMNS)
Holds the instance credential privately and injects it as X-PL-Agent / X-PL-Agent-Key on every coordination call — never from model arguments
The explicit state path is the only resume key: opened O_EXCL/O_NOFOLLOW at owner-only permissions, never overwritten; a failed or cancelled first register releases its empty reservation
60s attachment lease renewed by a 20s heartbeat task; a request retries at most twice (5xx and 429) before the adapter degrades

Registers resumable = a state path exists; note_turn() marks a forwarded tool call and the next heartbeat carries active:true, dropped for the process after one unexpected_parameter from an older daemon

Renders a per-turn digest from the pending_preview that attach/heartbeat return; the watermark moves only when the text changes; with a digest_path (host session id) the file and its .seen marker are what the prompt hooks read, and deliver_hint() hands each change to a tool result once plus a one-line reminder every HINT_REPEAT_CALLS while mail stays pending

An outage pauses the stream and the heartbeat task re-attaches with backoff (1 s to 60 s), replaying unacknowledged mail under the new generation; a restored notice follows the once-per-outage warning
inbox() long-polls receive (wait_seconds 30), marks one attempt per message per attachment and frames every event with a fixed agent-origin header; acknowledgment stays an explicit model action

v49: the daemon decides, the shim rings. The adapter declares its ring path (a digest for the Stop hook, or a Codex doorbell) in its register capabilities and as attach's ring, dropping the parameter once for a pre-v48 daemon; a wake on an attach or heartbeat answer (taken once, repeats ignored) becomes <key>.ring (digest watermark, then decision and reason) at ring_at for the Stop hook, and ring_due() offers the same ring to the Codex doorbell once due, dropped when its mail was already seen or nothing is pending; <key>.agent names the address for the park gate and is touched with the digest; .ring, .agent and the hooks' .turn leave with the digest and are swept with it
Declares exactly one experimental capability, claude/channel; no mailbox, host launch or implicit receipt
Serializes every outbound write through one lock, so events never interleave with tool replies on the shared stdout
Delivery starts only after the client's notifications/initialized; an out-of-order notification cannot open the inbox early
The caller supplies the inbox and this module owns only that worker's lifetime — stream submission is not proof of host receipt
Refuses non-loopback bind without token (exit 2) unless TRUST_BIND=1
Starts durability autosave, dream sweep, idle-session reaper
/health does a LIVE db ping on a dedicated connection

Reports status: degraded + init_refusal when the engine refuses for good (v25 dim guards; the shim exits on it), or degraded + not_ready while a retry can clear it (bank writer lease held elsewhere, failed store hydration backing off)

Startup also starts the stored-principal refresher and the release-check thread (PyPI once per updates.check_interval_seconds, 6 h; served on /health updates and in the briefing's update notice); a moved bank's old daemon refuses to start (exit 2)
Route order: /health → /ui → /api/hook/* → /api/pair → /api/* → /mcp
Bearer token; tokenless = loopback Origin/Host guard (CSRF / DNS-rebind)
POST must be exactly application/json (forces CORS preflight)
Sync service calls always via run_in_executor — never blocks the loop

POST /api/pair is the one unauthenticated write (pairing-code redemption): any Origin 403, one uniform 400 pairing_refused for every refused code, a failure budget then 429; stored (invited) principals are refused the operator POST paths
Every tool is a thin tier-tagged wrapper over MemoryService
_async_offload: tool bodies run on worker threads
tools/list filtered per principal tier; hidden tools stay callable server-side

Core memory_agents and memory_message delegate to coordination.py; mailbox authority requires bearer plus private adapter instance binding; dispatch raises CoordinationRefused (a ValueError: public code, optional detail such as an ambiguous prefix's candidates, text code: detail) and notifies each recipient a send's receipts name, so a burst or a prefix send wakes the right adapters
Resolution: principal override → tier map → stored principal's tier → env default (unset = full; compose sets core)
12h-TTL principal overrides (PrincipalTierState); visibility is a token lever, NOT security
core = 24 of 38 tools; minimal = 9; mailbox operations additionally require an adapter-held instance credential
A NAMED principal from the bearer token outranks X-PL-Writer (2026-08-10)
Then: X-PL-Writer / X-PL-Session → hook pointer → legacy mcp-session-id
mcp-session-id removed from MCP spec 2026-07-28 — fallback only
A presented bearer that resolves to no principal raises PrincipalsUnavailable instead of falling back to default
PSEUDOLIFE_MCP_TOKENS (token:principal,…) parsed fail-closed; malformed entries skipped
Matched principal IS the writer id and keys the toolset tier
Singular PSEUDOLIFE_MCP_TOKEN → reserved principal 'default' (legacy writer path kept)

Stored principals (v53, principal_store): resolved after the environment from an in-memory snapshot keyed by token SHA-256, refreshed every 10 s off the event loop; 503 principals_unavailable when never loaded or older than 60 s
principal_admitted(cfg, principal): the one board admission check (allowed_principals, or a stored row with board on); stored principals are refused POST /api/config and /api/daemon-notice
Hand-enumerated (method,path) → handler; NO generic tool proxy
/api/overview = one-round-trip dashboard aggregate
Serves the /api/briefing fast-path used by briefing_cli

Serves the session's memory_policy variant (compact = STARTUP_MEMORY_CORE inline; full_separate_hook = the full block on /api/hook/memory-policy; none; optional A/B arms), then a byte-bounded briefing; MEMORY_LOOP_BLOCK ≡ examples/CLAUDE.memory.md (guard-tested byte-identity) is the detailed standing copy
Authorized: registers active session + prepends the episode handle; the registration upserts the session's client_sessions row (v43) with the policy variant served
Unauthorized callers get byte-identical public output — no identity minting
An update, version or hooks-digest notice leads the output, for unauthorized callers too

Every dispatch runs on the hub's own 4-thread pool behind a 16-permit semaphore — never on the loop's default executor the console routes share, never on the event loop
A waiting receive subscribes to an asyncio.Event OUTSIDE the service lock and clears it BEFORE reading durable state, so a commit during the read cannot fall into a race gap
Caps: 30s wait, 64 waiters, one wait per (agent, attachment, generation) — a second is refused, not queued
A wait timeout still re-reads the authoritative database, covering a restart or any writer outside this loop
Shielded jobs own their capacity until the synchronous work ends; a disconnected caller cannot release it early
Owns CMS, cortex, world, lessons, graph, refbank and episodes
Dream + deep-dream methods live in service_dream.py (DreamOps mixin — one class, one lock at runtime)
_resolve_writer: X-PL-Session → hook pointer (6h TTL) → legacy header
PersistenceError counter surfaces save failures via /health

CPU precision cpu_dtype auto: bf16 loaded directly on native-bf16 CPUs, else fp32; rows leave as float32

Write-through to Postgres; .pt fallback schema v7 persists entry IDs, dream state, bank secret and display cursor together

Opt-in continuum preset: 8 tiers, promotion cadence, demotion cascade

Then negation / replacement / state-transition / NLI paths

Pure assembly — no LLM, no torch
Unsure-abouts + avoid-first lessons + fresh world facts + last-episode recap

Peer awareness in the full briefing whenever coordination is on (the default); the session-start hook leaves peers out (the board has its own hook); labels are context, not identity, and last reported activity is not liveness

Per-fact freshness_class (v23) · set-valued slots (v26) · epistemic stance (v29, latest-asserting-write, never a ranking input) · asserted_at/age on recall

~28 sub-configs; unknown YAML keys ignored

coordination.enabled defaults on (bearer authentication still required); awareness_limit bounds peer summaries; without the key allowed_principals admits the singular-token principal default plus bank-stored principals with board on; other token-map principals must be listed; audit_retention_days (default 90, 0 = forever) bounds the board audit log

Bearer principal must be admitted (listed in coordination.allowed_principals, or a stored principal with board on); every action except context, register and the leases listing also needs the adapter's X-PL-Agent / X-PL-Agent-Key headers
Per-action parameter allow-lists reject unexpected or missing parameters before any database work

Runs the store on a dedicated mailbox connection under the coordination lock; the service lock is used for cold durable-tier initialization and for full initialization before send, including clock-reseed retries; initialized mailbox calls avoid it, so a dream holding it cannot expire an adapter lease; send waits for clock history before stamping the message
Failures re-raise through public_error, so callers see a stable code and never a supplied value
The prune pass (at most once a minute, on register, send or heartbeat) hands coordination.audit_retention_days to the store
Disabled configuration answers {enabled: false} rather than an error, so a disabled bank stays quiet
unavailable_reason applies the same gates (enabled, bearer, listed principal, PostgreSQL) without storage I/O; GET /api/hook/coordination-start serves the startup check-in only when it returns none

v45 lease actions: lease (acquire, renew or queue), release, and leases, a listing the bearer alone may read; memory_agents claim/release map onto them with a day's ttl for claim:<path> and an hour otherwise, and update's expect sets a status's expected end; update's children (up to 8 labels, [] clears) names the subagents running under the caller's address, which only the parent may write

v49: update's park_reason/park_needs/park_clear_by/park_resume/park_expires and send's clears/urgent pass the allow-lists; park_gate() serves GET /api/hook/park-gate (allow or block plus PARK_GATE_MESSAGE) behind the same gates as the check-in, open on any failure; woke() serves POST /api/hook/woke (ok when the store recorded the marker, empty otherwise) behind the same gates; the store is built with the configured coordination.wake caps; the park request reaches sessions through memory_agents' description and the park gate (PARK_CHECKIN_SENTENCE stays out of CHECKIN_TEXT until a bench run)

v50: register's parent_thread passes the allow-list (a Codex native subagent's parent); invalid_parent and child_send_refused are public codes (child_send_refused is a 403 on REST); subagent() serves POST /api/hook/subagent?agent=<id>&event=start|stop&child=<agent_id>&type=<agent_type> for the plugin's SubagentStart/SubagentStop hooks behind the same gates as woke(): ok when the store recorded it, empty otherwise, open on any failure

nodes.s: agent rows + addressed mail + audit log
d: send locks both agent rows FOR UPDATE in agent-ID order, so reciprocal sends cannot deadlock each other
(sender, request_id) is the idempotency key: a repeat with the same fingerprint returns the first receipt, a different one is request_conflict
receive is cursor-based and non-destructive — ordered by per-recipient sequence, nothing is consumed until ack or expiry
ack takes one message_id or several comma-separated (MAX_PAGE): a batch returns receipts in order plus the ids that were not this mailbox's, under the agent row lock so overlapping batches serialize

Receive continuity explains expired unacknowledged mail and seven-day metadata gaps without expired bodies; authenticated history pages retained sends for this instance, with exact peer filtering, separate cursors, audit retention and operator redaction, and no delivery effects. v52 seeks sender and recipient pages separately, gets cursor high-water from two indexed heads and reconstructs only page message lifecycles through the message index; history and Console pin transactions and use transaction-local statement timeouts to bound lock occupancy for large caller-owned histories

console_snapshot uses a repeatable-read, read-only transaction over roster, unsettled leases, principal-visible pending counts and a bounded metadata-only event timeline; it never receives mail or settles a lease

v48: to, reply_to and ack's message ids resolve from a unique prefix of 8-31 lowercase hex characters (is_id_prefix; ambiguous_recipient / ambiguous_message_id / ambiguous_reply carry the candidates' distinguishing prefixes in CoordinationError.detail; to resolves among unrevoked addresses, reply_to and ack among the caller's own mail); to project:<name> or all reaches every attached non-idle peer but the sender (the adapter_available rows of list_agents, _fanout_rows), at most FANOUT_MAX (50), atomically under one request id whose fingerprint covers the resolved address, one row and one send event (payload fanout: {to, recipients}) with its own salt per recipient, counted once against SEND_RATE (distinct request ids); the sender and every recipient are locked in id order after an unlocked read of the set, which is re-read under the locks; send receipts carry recipient_agent_id, the stored wake decision and a path (live for an attached wake-enabled peer, else pull); resolve_agent_id serves the operator CLIs (export --agent against addresses and the log, rebind --agent among registered addresses, revoked included)
Conservative experiment bounds: 8 KB bodies, 256 pending, 60 sends/minute, 24h bodies, 7-day request keys
The coordination_hlc_highwater meta row only ever moves forward (numeric compare), so pruning mail cannot regress mailbox stamps
Live delivery is bounded to MAX_ATTEMPTS (3) per message across attachments; the adapter's receive skips exhausted mail, an explicit receive still returns it

prune() removes an address with no retained message once it has had neither its own activity nor a lease for seven days, or one hour when registered resumable:false; a heartbeat renews the lease but is activity only with active:true, and a re-attach under the row's own attachment_id is lease recovery, not activity; list_agents shows peers active within ACTIVE_WINDOW (ATTACHED_IDLE_WINDOW, 3 h, while leased), leased first, stamps each with status_set_at/status_age/status_stale (newest register or status update in the audit log, stale past STATUS_STALE_AFTER = 2 h) and counts the rest as idle_omitted

attach and heartbeat return pending_preview beside pending_count: the PREVIEW_LIMIT (5) oldest pending messages with sender label and a PREVIEW_EXCERPT (100-char) excerpt, read-only, for the shim's turn digest

Every mutation but a heartbeat or a plain lease renewal appends a coordination_events row in its own transaction: a dense seq under a transaction-scoped advisory lock taken last, hash = sha256(prev_hash || canonical row)

receive stamps first_read_at once, pull or delivery, and logs a read; prune logs expire/prune and, given audit_retention_days, cuts the log as a prefix and logs the cut (audit_prune) as the surviving chain's anchor

audit_events / verify_audit_chain back the operator-only board-audit CLI (export, verify and stats read one snapshot; redact writes; stats hands events, coordination_wakes rows and the suite lock's durations to board_audit_stats.compute_stats, which emits counts, seconds and names only); woke(agent, principal) logs the Stop hook's woke marker as a woke event counting the rings served to the address in the last hour; recover/rebind log operator events and still run on a restored pre-v42 bank, and on a pre-v46 one because only rows with a body name the body column

Resource leases (v45): acquire_lease is acquire, renew, or queue once; a freed lease goes to the head of its queue for LEASE_GRANT_WINDOW (300 s, or the waiter's ttl if shorter) and passes on if not renewed; every grant takes a fence from one sequence; grants, releases, expiries and operator breaks are audit events, renewals are not

Every lease mutation, ordinary board listing and prune settles due leases first; the Console read-only snapshot leaves expired holds unsettled, locking the lease row, then waiter rows, then the agent row, then the chain; prune never removes a live holder and deletes a departed waiter's queue rows

Redactable bodies (v46): a send event keeps its body in coordination_events.body, outside the hash, and its hashed payload commits to text_commitment (sha256 of a per-message salt in body_salt plus the body; no length); redact() (operator-only, never dispatched) locks the message row, then the chain, then blanks the body and the live copy and appends a redact event naming the send's seq (audit_copy removed) and returns the new head; a pre-v46 send keeps text in the payload, so only its live copy is taken (audit_copy kept); verify fails body_mismatch (a body its row does not commit to, or one back after its redaction), body_missing (absent without a later operator redact that removed it) or body_not_exported (an export with no body fields); redact clears body and body_salt together (a salt left alone too) and blanks the live row's request fingerprint, and takes the fingerprint even after a short audit retention cut the send event (audit_copy gone); after the commit the board-audit CLI runs VACUUM (ANALYZE) on both tables and vacuums pg_statistic, because ANALYZE copies sampled bodies, salts and fingerprints into the planner statistics; a step Postgres skips with a WARNING (a role without the privilege) is collected by a notice handler and reported as vacuumed false

looks_like_secret refuses credential-shaped message bodies and request ids, statuses, child labels, labels, projects, tasks, episodes, lease names and purposes, and redaction reasons with secret_like_body before the store reads or writes anything for the call, never echoing the text

v49 park record: update's park_* fields set it (park_reason in done/blocked/needs_approval/needs_info/needs_resource/waiting_peer; needs and clear_by 120 chars, resume 240; expires an epoch), a null reason or a status without park fields clears it, a field alone needs a standing park; park_gate(agent, principal, since) answers the Stop hook: a live standing park allows unless coordination_wakes has a rung delivery to this agent after since and park_set_at is not strictly later than the newest such delivery (a delivery is its send time, or served_at for a queued no-path ring); without a live park, the current-turn status/park update check and done-shaped status rule still apply, block otherwise

v49 wake decision at send (_wake_decision, on the locked recipient row): hinted while an unparked recipient acted within active_seconds (a parked one is decided on its park); a done park rings only for urgent mail from the maintainer, the maintainer's delegate for the project or its named clearer (reopened), else not_needed with reopen_by, and maintainer / delegate urgency spends authority_per_sender_per_hour; no_path without a live channel or a ring path (capabilities.ring, set by attach's ring); parked with a need: rung for the clearer, anyone, a clears naming the need in whole words or urgent (each within its cap), else withheld with the need; idle unparked (or a lapsed park): rung (reason urgent) for urgent within the same urgent sender cap, else not_needed (no_park), no ring and no row (regular mail never wakes, 2026-10-02; the hourly nudged ring is retired, and a nudged row from before is never served nor delivered live); per-recipient hourly and nightly caps, urgent per sender per hour, ring_at staggered across one sender's burst; each ring is a coordination_wakes row that the recipient's attach and heartbeat answers carry as wake: queued mail and Codex offers until ack or expiry, other rings for WAKE_SERVE_REPEAT (25 s) after first served; unparked urgent Codex mail is capped attention with no steer path

v50 subagents: register(parent_thread=) on a Codex row (capabilities name codex, episode is the thread) links the row to the most recently active live Codex row for that thread under the same principal (_codex_parent), and a Codex row registering links every row naming its thread (_link_children, one daemon update event per child, before = the row it replaced); prune clears parent_agent_id of the children of a removed parent; send from a row with parent_thread raises child_send_refused before any lookup; _public carries parent_agent_id and subagent. children entries with an agent_id belong to the hooks: subagent_started/subagent_stopped (actor hook) add or remove one by agent_id, labelled <agent_type>#<id8>, idempotent, with their own MAX_HOOK_CHILDREN (8, the oldest replaced past it) outside the parent's MAX_CHILDREN; a parent update keeps them (_parent_children) and is never refused because of them; _live_children hides a hook entry past HOOK_CHILD_TTL (the attached-idle window) and every write drops it; detach clears them all (a daemon update event); a refused children update applies nothing and says so

Operator grant: grant_delegate grants the lease delegate:<project> (reason delegate); a session asking for a delegate: or designated: (the 0.16.0 name) lease gets reserved_lease, a freed grant never passes to a queued session, a delegate: hold counts only with the operator's lease_delegate audit record for its current fence (so one a session took under 0.16.0 grants nothing), and a 0.16.0 designated:coordinator: hold grants nothing

nodes.s: pseudolife-mcp move · the bank to another host
d: Run on the source Docker-tier host; the target is a checkout host reached over key-based ssh (BatchMode); preflight refuses a target bank that is not empty (entries, facts or principals) or shares the source's bank fingerprint

Stops the source (docker stop, never rm), takes a final pg_dump and fences the database (ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false), copies with a SHA-256 check, restores with ops/restore.sh --apply --no-start; /data/move.json and /data/moved.json keep either daemon from starting outside the move

Carries the environment token identities over ssh stdin (--no-keep-tokens skips), starts the target once, then re-points this machine with connect; a failure or signal while the source is down rolls back in a fixed order, recorded under ~/.pseudolife-mcp/moves/<id>/

nodes.s: re-point client registrations at a daemon
d: Plan → confirm → verify → apply, all or nothing, across claude-code / codex / claude-desktop / gemini registrations and the hooks' URL + token-file copies; every file backed up and read back; never creates a registration

Verify = the shim's token-file check, an authenticated no-redirect request and an MCP handshake with the board check-in off, before anything is written; a remote target gets PSEUDOLIFE_MCP_NO_SPAWN=1; Codex is written through its app-server (codex_connection)
--code / --read-code joins a bank: runs pair only after confirmation (--dry-run never spends a code), then connects with the new token file

nodes.s: join a bank with one short code (v53)
d: invite <name> on the daemon host writes a principals row holding only the code's SHA-256 and prints the code once (15 min default, 24 h cap; --tier, --no-board, --list, --revoke, --replace); refuses unless the local daemon reports auth on and its /health bank fingerprint matches the database

pair on the joining machine mints its own token into a new owner-only file and sends POST /api/pair {code, token_sha256}: the token never crosses the wire; the answer names principal, tier and bank, and the file becomes ~/.pseudolife-mcp/<principal>.token

/api/pair sits before the bearer gate: any Origin is 403, JSON only, every refused redemption the same 400 pairing_refused (no oracle for which codes exist), a global budget of 20 failed redemptions a minute before 429
expose tailscale | off | status: tailscale serve --bg --tcp=<port> tcp://127.0.0.1:<port>, a raw TCP forward; client URL http://<tailnet ip>:<port>

Refuses unless local /health answers auth: true (a tunnel to loopback looks local and bypasses the bind guard); never replaces another serve or a Funnel on the port; undoes a forward that does not show up
The bank-fingerprint probe through the tailnet URL is advisory: a failure is reported, nothing rolled back

setup / status / doctor / verify / run / start / stop / shim / service / update over saved profiles; tunnel_runtime installs OpenAI's tunnel-client (0.0.15, SHA-256-pinned per OS/arch) and runs it with a profile whose MCP command is the stdio shim

tunnel_bridge launches the shim with a scrubbed environment (the profile's token file, OPENAI_API_KEY dropped) and writes payload-free receipts for memory_search / memory_agents; verify prints a nonce prompt to paste into the cloud app

tunnel_profiles keeps secret-free profile JSON plus <name>.key (DPAPI-wrapped on Windows, owner-only elsewhere) under ~/.pseudolife-mcp/tunnel; tunnel_service installs systemd / launchd / schtasks autostart only with --accept-autostart or --persistent

public.principals keeps only SHA-256 of the token and the pairing code, plus tier (minimal / core / full), board flag, code expiry, paired_at and revoked_at; environment names always shadow stored rows

PrincipalRefresher reloads the in-memory PrincipalSnapshot every 10 s on its own connection, never under the service or coordination lock nor on the event loop; resolution is one dict lookup by token hash

redeem() is one conditional UPDATE on the database clock (single use under concurrency; the same code + token hash retried within 600 s still answers); create_invite / list_principals / revoke back the invite CLI
CodexCoordinationRegistry attaches one coordination adapter per Codex thread (thread id only from the transport's _meta.threadId, a canonical UUID), private state under $CODEX_HOME/pseudolife/agents/

Doorbell: once the adapter's ring is due (rung or attention), the thread has been quiet 30 s and no earlier notice is unresolved, runs codex queue --thread <id> with fixed text (a count and a nonce) so peer text never enters a user turn; the woken model reads the mail with memory_message receive; any failure disables it for the process

codex_delivery (opt-in, PSEUDOLIFE_AGENT_WAKE plus a separate host token) pushes events to a loaded thread over a loopback app-server WebSocket and falls back to pull and the doorbell; codex_connection writes Codex's MCP config only through app-server config/batchWrite

nodes.s: judge opinions · automatic decisions · safe folds
d: review_judgments: one judge tick per queue (merge / link / junk); every pending opinion is fingerprinted to its evidence and judging policy; requeue clears pending opinions and never reopens a terminal decision

review_decisions: versioned audit of automatic nondestructive terminals only (merge or link reject, junk keep, candidate-pair dismissals), one meta row each plus a bounded active index; reopenable, and a human confirmation retires automatic ownership

curation_safety: lesson and world duplicate folds fail closed: automatic only on exact text with matching polarity and origin (world facts: equal citations, the survivor at least as fresh); the judge picks the survivor, never writes text, and the fold applies only if both rows still match the snapshot before and after row locking

run | hold | check | list | break | delegate (designate: deprecated alias); the truth is an OS file lock (os_lock, ~/.pseudolife-mcp/locks) held while the command runs; the board mirrors it through POST /api/coordination/lease | release | leases and keeps the FIFO queue; without a daemon it is flock with a name
run takes the board lease first, then the OS lock, renewing every ttl/3; hold --while-pid covers a process it did not start; break and delegate are operator-only and open the bank directly
check exits 0 free, 1 held, 70 when the check itself failed, so a gate never reads a crash as held

export (JSON lines in chain order) · verify (walks the hash chain) · redact (one body, with a reason) · stats; reaches the bank directly with the database owner's credentials: no MCP tool, no REST route, never a bearer

stats (board_audit_stats.compute_stats, pure) reports mail latency, wake precision against coordination_wakes, park outcomes, sends per session-hour and suite-lock waits as counts, seconds and names only
Exit 0 ok, 1 chain broken or redaction refused, 2 nothing checked or changed

One JSON report: installed versions, credential source, /health (2 s cap), an MCP stdio handshake (instructions, tool count, annotations), wake state, Codex hooks, coordination snapshot, saved tunnels; exit 0 only when ok
Never starts a daemon; a daemon/shim version mismatch sets ok false and recommends update --clients-only --tag <daemon version>
--agent-state adds a read_only POST /api/coordination/context; --disposable-proof is the one writing mode and needs an explicit PSEUDOLIFE_TEST_DATABASE_URL
update --schedule HH:MM registers a Task Scheduler task (Windows) or a systemd --user timer (Linux) running update --unattended once a day; --unschedule removes it; refused on the pip tier

Applies a release only when /health updates.unattended_daemon is on and the board lists no active session; takes the update lock, re-checks the board after the backup and before the rollback tag moves, then posts POST /api/daemon-notice
Exit 0 updated · 3 current · 4 held off · 2 could not check · 1 failed; every run appends to ~/.pseudolife-mcp/unattended-update.log

nodes.s: pseudolife-mcp update · the one deploy implementation
d: Release mode: newest PyPI version → refuse a downgrade → docker pull the GHCR daemon image → backup → rollback tag <current>-pre-update-<stamp> → prune → compose up -d --no-deps pseudolife-daemon (GHCR overlay) → health expecting that version → clients (not with --daemon-only)

Checkout mode (--checkout; what ops/update.* run): clean-tree guard (--allow-dirty) → backup → rollback tag → prune → HEAD re-checked → up -d --no-deps --build with git sha / dirty / build time stamped → health → clients only with --all → BuildKit cache prune

Held under an OS update.lock in the data dir (busy = exit 2); backup is the checkout's backup script, else a built-in in-container pg_dump + /data tar; exit 1 daemon failure, 2 could not run, 3 current, 5 client step failed

nodes.s: moves shim, plugin cache and Codex hooks together
d: Shim: installs a numbered side-by-side runtime (venv, pip --no-deps, version probe, runtime.json written last) behind one stable launcher, migrates registrations to the launcher (each file backed up) and removes runtimes nothing names or runs
Plugin: claude plugin marketplace update, a byte compare of marketplace clone and cache, claude plugin update only on a difference, then the compare again as proof; never uninstalls
Codex: refreshes manual hook copies, upgrades a plugin copy via codex plugin marketplace upgrade, prints re-approval steps only when an approved hook definition changed; saved tunnels are updated too

edges.l: flat band (promotion walk under multi-band presets)
attaches by default when the daemon serves the shim's bearer the board (PSEUDOLIFE_AGENT_COORDINATION=0 opts out) · wake only with PSEUDOLIFE_AGENT_WAKE
channel mode · serve_channel owns the connection
CoordinationStore on its own connection under the coordination lock
deploy_release while the board is idle
claude plugin update (on a byte difference)
codex queue wakes the idle thread
vendor client runs the shim via the bridge

store.name: store
store.desc: memory_store: Claude Code → shim → /mcp → MemoryService → embed → CMS (contradiction check BEFORE the surprise gate) → the flat band + slot index → regex slot promotion into the cortex → write-through to Postgres.

recall.name: search / recall
recall.desc: memory_search & memory_recall: query embedded, then a 5-pool merge — the neural store + slot index + optional BM25 + reference bank + optional cross-encoder rerank. memory_recall wraps it in an iterative graph-hop loop.

dream.name: dream
dream.desc: The consolidation cycle: daemon sweep tick → compaction always, dream on backlog + quiescence → extractor LLM (Sonnet shim primary / sidecar fallback) → claims to cortex, lessons, relations to graph → insight digest refresh.

briefing.name: briefing
briefing.desc: SessionStart: plugin hook curls /api/hook/session-start → identity tier-3 registration + episode handle → briefing markdown assembled from graph digest, avoid-first lessons, fresh world facts, and the last episode recap.

console.name: console
console.desc: Cortex Console: browser loads the SPA from /ui/, then REST-only calls through the auth gate into the hand-enumerated route table — no generic tool proxy exists for the browser surface.

deploy.name: deploy
deploy.desc: Lifecycle: install (preflight → compose up → hooks). Updates run through pseudolife-mcp update (ops/update.* wrap its checkout mode): backup → rollback tag → daemon-only --no-deps recreate → health poll → client side (shim runtime, plugin cache, Codex hooks). The distilled E4B model is the one eval artifact baked into a shipped image.
